# THE PREMORTEM: Why Origin/Main Broke

## THE FAILURE STORY

By February, six months after the July work was committed, the first integration test against origin/main failed silently. The 43 unmerged commits from the 10 worktrees—the real implementation of system_v5 and system_v7 refactoring—never made it to main. Instead, what landed was the v9 scaffolding commit: 6,637 lines of JSON configuration stubs defining class signatures, function names, import paths. The Python beneath it was hollow: 1,234 lines of `pass`, empty methods, stub return values. The July work—real business logic, database adapters, validation pipelines—lived in the worktrees at f0afdc36a and claimgate/bypass-regression. Nobody integrated them before the v9 scaffolding became canonical.

By March, when teams tried to consume main, they called methods that existed as signatures only. The JSON config was perfect scaffolding—architecture was sound, boundaries were clean, 28 of 33 CB light libraries wired correctly. But wiring doesn't execute. A request handler instantiated a processor class that existed only in JSON. Tests passed because they tested the schema, not the behavior. The 180 dirty files in the primary checkout—the actual working implementations—remained offline. The merge had "succeeded": no conflicts, clean cherry-pick of the skeleton onto main. No one had checked whether the skeleton had a spine.

By June, the discovery was brutal: rolling back v9 scaffolding was impossible without orphaning new schema dependents. The real July work had to be manually ported into the skeleton structure, line by line, because the branches had diverged too far. This wasn't a merge failure. It was a commitment failure—the wrong artifact went to main.

## THE UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION

Merging a commit with clean history and valid JSON syntax meant the commit was production-ready; no one verified the Python actually executed.

## EARLY WARNING SIGNS

1. **v9 commit is 85% JSON, 15% Python.** Before merge, ask: where is the implementation? This ratio is a red flag at review time, not at deployment time.

2. **The 10 worktrees remain unmerged past July 18.** By day 7 post-implementation, integration branches should be merging or failing visibly. Silence means they're orphaning.
